items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Well it’s like referring to Marian McPartland as “one of the best of the women jazz musicians.”

ctx.x: Yeah. Still. Yeah. It happens. And does it happen less? I’m sure it happens less. But does it still happen? Yeah. It doesn’t bother me. I still work. I still travel and maybe I don’t want to work with them. Do you know what I mean? It’s like I don’t really care so much about the politics anymore as long as I’m playing with good people and as long as I have the respect of the musicians that I admire. I mean really who cares in the end. You know what I mean? If you start worrying about the gigs you’re not doing it…
Well it’s like referring to Marian McPartland as “one of the best of the women jazz musicians.”

Yeah. And still today. You know and certain clubs that shall remain nameless, but trying to get a gig there is, you might get a night on a “Woman in Jazz” week. You know and it’s kind of like wow, you still have those? Well I guess we do. And Billy Taylor has a wonderful Woman in Jazz Festival at the Kennedy Center. You know, but he’s doing it for the right reason. He’s doing it because he wants to highlight women leaders more. You know, so it’s not only women playing.
